title: Local social cohesion can remain resilient while system-level pessimism and institutional distrust intensify political vulnerability
source_unit: UNDP Bosnia and Herzegovina, Social Cohesion and Reconciliation (SCORE) Index 2025 executive summary
geography: Bosnia and Herzegovina, all 16 regional-territorial units, with comparison to SCORE 2020 and contextual reference to 2014 and 2020 waves

denominator.unit: approximately surveyed respondents including 660 booster respondents; nationally representative weighted sample approximately 3,170

core_elements.value: intergroup harmony, inclusive belonging, sense of progress, support for Bosnia and Herzegovina institutions, and constructive citizenship

fieldwork.value: November 2025 to February 2026, with most data collected in November-December 2025

observations.method: UNDP and SeeD use a stratified, face-to-face CAPI survey across all regional-territorial units, with a weighted nationally representative sample and local booster sites.
observations.uncertainty: The index is a national social-cohesion survey, not a complete account of informal networks or local power; the 2020 comparison coincided with COVID-19 and should be interpreted cautiously.
observations.subgroup: Residents across entities, ethnic and demographic groups, regional-territorial units, civic institutions, and communities experiencing post-conflict governance and reconciliation pressures.
observations.counterinterpretation: Moderate national cohesion does not imply equal safety, trust, political inclusion, or intergroup experience across all communities and localities.

observations.period: 2025; lived local relations and community-level cooperation

local_cooperation.value: strong community cooperation at the local level

inclusive_identity.value: inclusive civic identity and identification with Bosnia and Herzegovina remain sufficiently strong to serve as an enabling platform

observations.method: The report synthesizes SCORE dimensions and weighted survey findings into a national interpretation of everyday relations, belonging, and cooperation.
observations.uncertainty: Qualitative labels such as moderate, above-average, and strong summarize index results; they do not identify which mechanisms caused cohesion or guarantee durability under future shocks.
observations.subgroup: Neighbors, communities, civic actors, residents with different identities, and institutions that support local cooperation and inclusive belonging.
observations.counterinterpretation: Positive local interaction can coexist with segregation, unequal opportunity, weak institutional trust, or limited political influence.

observations.period: 2025; system-level perceptions of direction, stability, and economic future

pessimism.value: pessimism about the country's direction remains widespread

perceived_drivers.value: political instability, economic uncertainty, and regional dynamics

local_system_gap.value: relatively positive local experiences coexist with negative system-level perceptions

observations.method: The executive summary compares local social experience and system-level perceptions within the SCORE framework and relates the gap to civic engagement and vulnerability to divisive narratives.
observations.uncertainty: The report identifies an association and interpretive pathway, not a causal estimate that pessimism directly produces disengagement or susceptibility to divisive narratives.
observations.subgroup: Residents evaluating national institutions, political direction, economic security, regional stability, civic participation, and public narratives.
observations.counterinterpretation: System-level pessimism may coexist with active civic engagement, local problem-solving, or mobilization rather than only withdrawal and vulnerability.

observations.period: 2020-2025; change in social-cohesion elements and post-pandemic comparison

denominator.unit: SCORE comparison across the 2020 and 2025 waves

comparison_waves.value: 2020 and 2025, with SCORE also implemented in 2014

reported_improvements.value: improvements in intergroup harmony, constructive civic action, and support for Bosnia and Herzegovina institutions are reported in public summaries

baseline_caveat.value: 2020 coincided with the COVID-19 period and may represent an unusually low baseline

observations.method: SCORE compares repeated national measurements while noting the unusual context of the 2020 wave and differences in fieldwork timing and local coverage.
observations.uncertainty: Repeated cross-sectional comparisons do not follow the same individuals and cannot isolate cohort, period, sampling, or pandemic effects from genuine social change.
observations.subgroup: Residents, institutions, communities, and civic actors observed across repeated national social-cohesion measurement waves.
observations.counterinterpretation: Apparent improvement can reflect recovery from an exceptional pandemic baseline, changing expectations, or measurement context rather than a durable reconciliation trend.

related_sources.claim: SCORE project scope, public data, social-cohesion measurement, and implementation context.

boundary: This record adds a regional social-cohesion route linking local cooperation, inclusive belonging, system-level pessimism, institutional support, civic action, and vulnerability to divisive narratives. It uses an aggregate interpretation of a weighted national survey, not individual respondent histories, a causal political-behavior evaluation, a complete account of local power, or evidence that resilience will persist under future shocks.

reproduction_audit.retrieval_hash_scope: Official UNDP SCORE 2025 executive summary, publication page, project page, and methodology context were reviewed for the sample and coverage frame, five core elements, local-resilience findings, local/system perception gap, repeated-wave comparison, and COVID-2020 baseline caveat.
